transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
I’m… a little embarrassed to say it. I’ve been having thoughts that it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow. I don’t have a plan to hurt myself, but it scared me enough to come in.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up tomorrow?
About eight months, I think. Since my brother’s health—and his behavior—changed so suddenly. It’s been… on and off since then.
Have you noticed any changes in the things you enjoy doing since these thoughts started?

Yes… I suppose so. I still get my watercolor things out sometimes, but then I just sit there looking at the blank paper. The pleasure I used to get from the colors and the light… it just doesn’t really come, so I put it all away again.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

Not many, no. I still try with my watercolors sometimes… I’ll set everything out, but then I just stare at the paper. The feeling I used to get from the colors, the light… it doesn’t really come, so I end up putting it away.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or how quickly you move compared to before these thoughts started?
I’m not sure… I haven’t really noticed anything definite like that. Maybe I’m a bit slower some days, but I couldn’t say for certain.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?

Yes… I do. I keep thinking about my brother, how he was declining, and I tell myself I should have noticed sooner. That maybe if I’d been a better sister… more attentive… I could have prevented some of it.
Do you feel like you're moving more slowly than usual most of the time?
I don’t really know. I haven’t paid close enough attention to say it’s most of the time. Some days I probably am, but… I’m not sure.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight since these thoughts started?
I haven’t really noticed a significant change. My clothes seem about the same, I think… I haven’t been checking my weight much.
Do you feel like you're resting or sleeping more than you used to?

Not more, no. If anything it doesn’t feel restful. I fall asleep… sort of unevenly, and then I’m awake around three or four thinking about calls, forms, whether I handled things right. By morning it feels like I barely rested.
Do you feel like your movements or reactions are slower than they used to be most of the time?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed that clearly… maybe sometimes I’m a bit slower, but I couldn’t say it’s most of the time.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in things most of the day?
Yes… I think so. Most days it’s like there’s this grayness over everything. Even simple things, like making tea or looking out at the garden, feel heavy somehow. It’s hard to shake.
Are there any things that you used to enjoy but no longer find pleasure in?

Yes… my watercolors, mostly. I still take them out sometimes, but I just sit there looking at the blank paper. The feeling I used to get from the colors… it doesn’t really come, so I usually put it all away.
Are there any activities that still bring you joy or pleasure?

Not much, really. I suppose I still try with my watercolors sometimes… I set everything out, but then I just stare at the paper. The pleasure I used to get from the colors and the light just… doesn’t seem to come, so I put it away.
How long have you been feeling this grayness over everything most of the day?
About eight months, I think. Since my brother’s health and… behavior changed so suddenly. It’s been hard to get back to feeling like myself.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

Not really. I mean… I still put out my watercolor things sometimes, but I just end up staring at the paper. The feeling I used to get from the colors and the light… it doesn’t seem to come, so I pack it away.
Do you feel like your movements are slower than usual?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed that, exactly… maybe I’m just doing less.
Do you feel like it takes you longer to do things than it used to?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but I haven’t really paid attention to the timing. Things just feel harder to start, I suppose.
Do you feel like it's hard to get started on things you need to do?

Yes… I suppose it is. I manage the things I have to do, the basics. But I’ve let go of my walking group, and I haven’t really kept up with mentoring. I just don’t seem to follow through, and when I’m with people I feel… not quite there.
Do you feel like it's hard to think clearly or make decisions?
I’m not sure… maybe sometimes. I can still decide things, I think, but it can feel a bit foggy. I haven’t really kept track of it.
Do you feel like it's hard to think or move when you're doing everyday activities?
I’m not sure I’d say that exactly. I haven’t really noticed moving slowly… everyday things just feel a bit more effortful, I suppose.
